To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
accelerated HIV testing in maternity and labour units is feasible and effective.
24 hours×7 day HIV testing in the maternity and labour wards in Malawi was a successful intervention to increase the coverage of women tested and identified with HIV.

1) HIV testing in maternity wards was associated with high coverage and uptake of HIV testing; 2) the coverage of PMTCT increased with the availability of HIV testing in the maternity ward and; 3) HIV testing in the labour ward is a good strategy for improving PMTCT coverage.

the effectiveness of round the clock (24/7) HIV testing and counselling (HTC) services for prevention of mother to Child Transmission (PMTCT).

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PMTCT coverage is high when most of the women delivering in health facilities have their HIV status known.
accelerated HIV testing is an important component of PMTCT and should be implemented in all maternity wards in Malawi and beyond.
accelerated HIV testing for PMTC is vital to capture the majority of mothers at a critical time of their life.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated that it is feasible to implement accelerated testing in the labour wards and that this can be done without compromising the quality of the service.
the introduction of accelerated HIV testing in maternity and labour ward in Malawi has been a great success.
HIV testing in labour and maternity wards should be accelerated to increase the PMTCT coverage and reduce the risk of mother to child HIV transmission.
The main takeaway from our work is that
accelerated HIV testing in maternity and labour ward is feasible and can be done round the clock.
the integration of HIV testing in the maternity ward can increase the coverage of PMTCT services.
HIV testing in maternity wards can be done 24 hours×7days and can be done with the support of trained lay counsellors.
